qa.plant_name: Paducah American Energy Hub gas plant
qa.question: Should the Paducah American Energy Hub gas plant stay at the former Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant point?
qa.finding: NextEra's fact sheet and the Kentucky Lantern say the gas plants will be built at or near the former Paducah plant in McCracken County. No permit or site plan gives a final point yet.
qa.recommendation: Keep the point as approximate at the former plant site and move it when an air permit application gives the site.
qa.researcher_notes: The fact sheet also lists up to 2.6 gigawatts of battery storage, which is not in scope. The fact sheet says the data center could reach 8 gigawatts.

verifications.note: NextEra fact sheet for the Paducah American Energy Hub. It says McCracken County, natural gas generation of up to 2,000 MW, and commercial operation as early as 2032.
Kentucky Lantern story of July 29, 2026. It says NextEra will install two gigawatts of natural gas-fired generation at or near the former Paducah plant in McCracken County.

qa.plant_name: EKPC Mason County gas plant (PJM C01-1227)
qa.question: Should East Kentucky Power Cooperative's PJM request C01-1227 be a new plant, or a new unit at Spurlock power station?
qa.finding: The request connects to the Spurlock to Meldahl Dam 345 kV line in Mason County, which starts at Spurlock. No filing names a site, and the cooperative's 2025 plan names no new Spurlock unit.
qa.recommendation: Add it as a new plant now, and move it to Spurlock as a new unit if a commission case puts it at the Spurlock site.
qa.researcher_notes: Meta's Crisham LLC campus is planned in the same county, so the request may serve it. The Spurlock plant's own research wrote a watch item for the same row; drop that one if this add is accepted.

qa.plant_name: Appalachian Power gas plant at Baker 345 kV (PJM C01-1325)
qa.question: Is Appalachian Power's PJM request C01-1325 in Lawrence County, Kentucky one of GEM's two Appalachian Power plan placeholders in West Virginia?
qa.finding: Yes, treat it as the same need. Appalachian Power's 2025 resource plan, filed October 1, 2025 in West Virginia case 25-0859-E-IRP, models a generic combined cycle plant of about 1,227 MW on PDF page 74 and adds about 1,200 MW of it in 2032, growing to about 2,500 MW by 2035, on PDF page 103. The plan names no site, so the West Virginia points of GEM's two placeholders are guesses, and requests C01-1325 and C01-1326 are how Appalachian Power is now trying to fill that need.
qa.recommendation: Do not add C01-1325 as a new Kentucky plant. Keep the two West Virginia placeholders and update their site, county, capacity and start year when Appalachian Power picks a site through its 2026 request for proposals or a certificate case.
qa.researcher_notes: GEM's placeholders are Appalachian Power 2025 IRP power station 1 and 2, L100001083287 and L100001083288, both 1,227 MW, approximate location, no county. The plan is the October 1, 2025 filing in West Virginia Public Service Commission case 25-0859-E-IRP. PDF page 74 describes the H-class 1,200 MW combined cycle option with a net capacity of approximately 1,227 MW. PDF page 98 says the plan does not pick a single preferred portfolio. PDF page 103 says about 1,200 MW of combined cycle is added after the coal units retire in 2032, expanding to around 2,500 MW by 2035. The plan names no site for any new plant. Appalachian Power then filed PJM request C01-1325 on April 24, 2026 for 1,046 MW of gas at Baker 345 kV in Lawrence County, Kentucky, and C01-1326 three days later for 1,045 MW of gas in Wayne County, West Virginia. Both list September 2031. The PJM project page names Appalachian Power, the Baker 345 kV point and status Active, but not the megawatts. The megawatts and county come from interconnection.fyi, a lead site. Appalachian Power's request for proposals dated August 14, 2026 seeks up to 1,500 MW of gas combined cycle in service by March 31, 2031, in section 2.1 and section 3.2. Section 7.2.2 gives preference to projects in West Virginia on Appalachian Power's own lines. The commission's order of September 14, 2026 in the same case names no site. Two requests near 1,045 MW fit either one plant with two site options or two plants matching the two placeholders. That decides which placeholder each request fits, not whether it is a new plant. Kentucky Power's 760 MW Lawrence County plant in Kentucky case 2026-00324 is a different utility and a different project.
